text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, you should choose clear, meaningful endpoints that describe your resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct status codes so clients understand what happened: use 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation helps other developers learn how to use your API quickly, so keep it up to date. Finally, plan for versioning from the start, for example by adding /v1/ to your URLs. This way, you can improve your API without breaking existing applications that depend on it.
